description: This line plot illustrates how the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—varies with increasing co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³ (1,000), with tick marks at 10⁰ (1), 10¹ (10), 10² (100), and 10³ (1,000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and spans from 60% to 80%. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 62% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rising to about 67% at 1,000. The "MEND" method, shown as a brown line with diamond markers, begins near 67% and increases to around 77%. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 64% and ends near 68%. The "MEMIT" method, indicated by a purple line with star markers, begins at roughly 66% and rises to approximately 75%. The "IKE" method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at about 66% and ends near 73%. The "ROME" method, represented by a green line with square markers, begins at approximately 74% and increases to about 81%.
